name: Saints Timothy and Titus
history: Two of Saint Paul’s closest companions, to whom he wrote the letters that bear their names. Timothy, son of a Jewish mother and a Greek father, travelled with Paul for years and was left in charge of the church at Ephesus. Titus, a Gentile convert, was sent to Corinth to make peace and then to Crete to organise the young Church there. Tradition counts them the first bishops of those places.
life: Paul met Timothy at Lystra, where the young man’s mother Eunice and grandmother Lois had taught him the Scriptures from childhood. Paul called him his beloved son and fellow worker, and sent him on difficult errands to Thessalonica, Corinth and Philippi. In his letters Paul urges him not to let anyone despise his youth, to take a little wine for his frequent ailments, and to guard what has been entrusted to him. Tradition holds that Timothy was killed at Ephesus for protesting against a pagan festival. Titus was a Greek whom Paul took to the council at Jerusalem as a sign that Gentiles need not be circumcised. Sent to Corinth after Paul had written them a severe letter, he came back with good news, to Paul’s great comfort. Left in Crete to appoint elders in every town, he is said to have died there in old age. The letters to them still guide bishops and pastors.
prayerTo: Saints Timothy and Titus, you learned the faith from Paul and handed it on whole. Pray for our bishops and priests, that they may preach the word in season and out of season. Pray for parents and grandparents who teach the faith at home, and for me, that I may guard what has been entrusted to me. Amen.
penance: Timothy learned the faith from his mother and grandmother. Thank someone who taught you the faith, and pray today for your bishop by name.
meditation: Paul told Timothy to stir into flame the gift of God that was within him. What gift has God given you that is burning low?
